english: Among the fallen and the broken of an ancient world, lies among them a single structure.
A monument to a forgotten power.
At the top, a cracked lion's head glares at you. A one-eyed lion, with a single dark and empty socket.
It's a shrine, isn't it?
A shrine, like any other. You feel at home on your knees here.
Of course you do.
Silence, degenerate.
A shrine to what god?
Does it... work?
M-(Take a step closer.)
Whitemane.
They lived here. Not first. Not last.
One lost to time.
You may prepare spells here, yes.
There is a connection. To divinity.
Somehow.
Shrines like this often hold a latent connection to Jor's Strings.
If you can do it at the shrine of one dead god, why not another?
Do not compare Urth to this cat-god.
If you think your god is somehow unique, then you are sorely mistaken.
Sure.
Looks like a normal cat-thing. There's a ton of them all over the city, if you know where to look.
Are you some type of cat expert?
Do I know where to look?
Go on.
No.
He speaks truth.
Clearly. You found this one.
I... don't have anything else to say, really.
Hard to tell exactly what's going on here, due to the rubble and the dust.
You could try investigating it more closely. But remember...
The Whitemanes are famous for their traps.
You know, like that fiery hallway you barely survived.
So be careful.
Your scarf rustles.
Meek thinks spooky ghost, his first comment is, before he even opens his eye. "Many spooky ghost in place like this."
The mimic's gaze darts around the chamber.
Yes-yes. One hundred percent - is trap here. Master beware!
Not surprising. If you gotta investigate, just... be careful.
I don't know why I even say that, I know you're not going to listen.
You can listen. Just not right now.
You look over the front of the shrine, seeing traces of markings on the surface.
You approach the ancient shrine.
What's that light from the ceiling?
Investigate the shrine.
(Prepare spells.)
E-(Nod your head.)
It is an illusion. Do not mind it.
It is absolutely not the sun.
Glancing upwards reveals the rays to be nothing but a magical tingle on your eyes.
This is no esoteric pocket- but it most likely once was.
A fake sun on ancient stone.
Like ALL of JOR.
Your gloved hand glides over the markings on the front of the shrine.
There's something there.
Inside the stone.
And it's...
Text.
Tracing your fingers, you realize something is written, faintly, scrubbed down over centuries, into the surface of the shrine.
It says, 'EL OJO ROJO VIGILA TUS LOGROS.'
It means, 'the red eye watches over you'.
You take a step back, and mumble it to yourself.
It means, 'the red eye-'
The red eye... watches over you.
Does that mean anything?
He shrugs. "They honestly might have. But... who knows?"
You glance upwards, at the lion's head.
The eye socket.
Perfectly sized for a gemstone. This is obviously a secret you would be able to trigger, in case you insert the correct gemstone.
(Look at the eye socket.)
Not now.
Fine. Later, then.
You trace your fingers over the markings at the front.
There's something here. Inside the shrine.
But you can't figure out how to possibly get it open.
This thick of a stone block would not be easy to destroy, even if you have a perfect tool for the job.
No, there is some other way...
But what?
You dust off the front of the shrine.
Then the sides of the shrine.
It's faint, but there is some type of symbol on it.
It's difficult to tell what's a weathered scratch, and what's a creative choice.
(Look closer.)
Yes.
A symbol.
A symbol of a sun. Definitely.
If this is what Akzel wanted you to find, you've found it.
Huh. So what do I do now?
Get back to your dwarf buddy, of course!
Hm. Yes.
Tell Akzel about this symbol. He would be grateful for the information.
Very grateful.
Like, get-a-nice-little-payday grateful.
You find what you're looking for?
I like the sound of that. I want a payday too.
Or maybe I'll just be happy that he's happy. We'll all be happy together.
I should get back to Akzel then, to those other ruins. Man, there's a lot of ruins down here.
Great. Happy for you.
His tone of voice indicates: 'please, please, can we leave this scary ruin now?'
Who doesn't?!
That sounds lovely.
Yes you should. Right away!
The stony lion's head glares at you with that one sunken, dark eye.
Do it! Put in that gem you found between the cow's legs!
Might want to be a bit careful about it, but you could probably put in that jacinth here...
(Poke your finger in the hole.)
I'm done checking out the eye socket.
Yes. Either a ruby, or a jacinth would be a rather practical guess.
These barbaric civilizations - if you can even call them that - were all the same. Shiny rocks in mysterious temples, used as esoteric triggers.
Indeed.
You do so, sticking it in.
First an inch. Then two.
Then your whole index finger.
This is a great way to lose a body part.
There are many tales of dark voids that consume any inserted limbs.
(Wiggle it around.)
(Take out your finger, and hope it remains attached to your hand.)
You do so.
For some reason.
Nothing happens...?
You feel the inside of the lion's head. It appears hollow.
The goblin stares at you - a questioning expression.
Slowly pulling out, your index luckily remains.
Phew...!
But something is missing...
Perhaps.
Perchance.
Carefully you guide the jacinth into the perfectly sized eye-hole.
Once close enough, like a magnet it gets sucked in.
Then you hear a strange noise in the walls.
OH GODS!
Mm?
Did something happen?
The goblin gasps for air, unable to speak.
(Look to your left.)
Oh.
You just almost - ALMOST - just DIED.
That was fast.
(Begin to shake, due to a slightly delayed adrenaline kick.)
You would have died, had the final blade not been blocked by those vines.
And Snell would have died if he had stood just a bit further back - or to the left.
...F-fuck...
The goblin is actually shaking.
We were...
We were so... close. To just, like... dying. Look at these things...! We'd be- you'd be- cut in half!
Are you aware of that, Cleric?
Hm? What's going on?
No. Real men don't process emotions like that.
Yes. Maybe. We'll see in a bit. (Shiver.)
There's magic for that. Like... Regenerate.
(Look around.) "What? Something happen?"
I see. You're a stoic, then.
All real men are.
Of course. Feelings don't faze me. (Feel a bit faint.)
You sure? You look a little-
I've heard a delayed response is normal in these situations.
Heard about a guy that got an arrow through his skull once. Like, straight through.
The goblin tends to talk a lot when he is in emotional panic.
This fucking guy, he just kept walking about like nothing had happened. Like he was just-
Regenerate? Like... the one used for lost limbs?
Don't you mean Revivify?
I almost just died, please don't argue semantics, Snell.
Look, I'm not the magic guy here, but-
You serious? Are you serious?! You don't see the- you didn't-
With a brash crack, the front of the shrine pops out of place.
The goblin jumps.
A deep rumbling voice echoes through the chamber, as a lion's skull begins floating out of the shrine, along with a ghostly halberd.
<shake>EL VIGILANTE ROJO DE CRINBLANCA, CASTIGARÁ TU-</shake>
Then the skull falls to the ground.
(Stare at it as it rolls to the side.)
Is that... it?
Huh.
I'm not sure?
He glances around, scanning for threats.
That was a ghostly apparition, left to guard this shrine.
Some kind of ghost?
Ghost-failure?
I don't think they planned it to go that way.
There we go. The undead spirit of this heretical temple has been vanquished. (Feel proud.)
For once I agree with you.
Huzzah.
Yeah. Great job.
I want to believe you.
The skull is on ground before you. And that halberd is just... floating there. All ghost-like.
Be careful.
Loot them. Come on.
E-Guess I'll... check them out.
